messages:
Anya: noticing a new pattern on one of the p99 hosts — KV residency keeps growing for a single tenant after longctx runs, even though eviction_rate is nonzero. logs attached below, short dump first.
Matt: can you paste the small dump?
Anya: sure — from vm_metrics: 
```\nkv_residency: 62.1%\neviction_ops: 1243\npagewalks: 5602\nfrag_ratio: 1.28\nactive_tenant: tenant-42\nlongctx_pct: 0.18\n```
Li: 62% residency isn't awful by itself, but pagewalks >> evictions is suspicious — looks like a lot of inactive pages getting visited but not freed.
Sara: is tenant-42 running the long-context batch we rolled out last week? that might keep more KV segments live.
Anya: yes they're the one running the >32k token conversation workloads. We also see repeated small spikes when their sessions end, not bulk frees.
Kevin: could be slab fragmentation plus reuse not matching our handoff granularity. If the tenant pins lots of longctx entries, small evictions won't free contiguous pages.
Matt: any pprof heap/profile traces?
Anya: grabbed an allocation profile during a reproduction: 
```\n# 10s heap profile snippet\nlost_pages_by_tenant: {tenant-42: 1345, tenant-7: 120, tenant-9: 90}\nhotspot: kv_page_table_lookup (40%), kv_kv_iterate (18%), pagewalk_linear_scan (12%)\n```
Li: kv_page_table_lookup 40% aligns with heavy pagewalk pressure. That function spending cycles suggests many small resident checks rather than bulk eviction.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: canary rollout `longctx-v2` to region-us-east completed at 2167890100 :white_check_mark:
Sara: hmm the canary timestamp matches when tenant-42 scaled up. Could be correlated.
Kevin: hypothesis: the batching heuristics for longctx requests are increasing concurrent KV writes, causing interleaved allocations that fragment slabs. Then our eviction scanner picks nonadjacent pages causing many pagewalks and slow reclaim.
Matt: what about quota boundaries? tenant quotas are 4GB by default, but tenant-42 has a burst policy to 6GB. Do we observe crossing the hard watermarks?
Anya: metrics show tenant-42 peaked ~5.7GB, did not hit hard limit. Per-tenant soft_quota_unavailable_count is higher though.
Li: soft quota triggers can alter eviction priority; if we're deprioritizing soft-tripped tenants in favor of others, that could make noisy residency persist. Need to check fairshare comparator.
Sara: can we reproduce locally with a stress script? I can spin up a shaded infra with smaller slab sizes to accelerate fragmentation.
Anya: repro steps I used: 
1) start 3 clients; 1 heavy longctx generator (tenant-42 equivalent), 2 small chatty tenants
2) use sequence lengths 12k-40k with intermittent continues (no explicit end)
3) run for ~20 minutes and watch kv_residency and pagewalk rate
Logs: we saw gradual residency climb for heavy tenant even after session close, with reuse_rate per slab dropping from 0.65 -> 0.18

Kevin: suggestions: a) implement slab compaction pass when fragmentation ratio > 1.2, b) increase eviction handoff coalescing window so adjacent reclaimed pages freed together, c) add a soft_quota smoothing timer so tenants only get burst credit if they sustained lower usage for X minutes.
Matt: for (b) how big should the coalescing window be? Too big and we might add latency to frees.
Kevin: start with 50ms grouping at eviction path and measure. It just batches reclaim requests to adjacent ranges. Shouldn't add tail latency for normal small frees.
Li: also consider changing our kernel selection hints: for workloads with longctx bursts we might prefer kernels that reduce pagewalk costs (fewer random accesses). The runtime can increase prefetch depth for tenants flagged as longctx-heavy.
Sara: preftech depth plus coalesced eviction could help. I'll prototype a tiny shim that tags a tenant's allocator with prefetch_hint=ON for heavy sessions.
Anya: another oddity — we saw many 'reuse_miss' counters incrementing for tenant-42 after we moved from qemu-optimized kernels to vectorized kernels last week. Could be change in allocation alignment.
Matt: that smells like a regression tied to the kernel selection change. Did we roll back any kernel experiments recently?
Anya: kernels rolled at 2167889000 across us-east; infra-change-log shows kernel-profile switch to fast-vector.
Li: schedule a repro with old kernel vs new kernel, same workload. If vectorized kernel shifted allocation offsets, fragmentation could increase. Quick A/B would confirm.
InfraBot: perf-runner: scheduled perf job 2167890250 comparing kernel-fast-vector vs kernel-qemu on shaded infra.
Kevin: if A/B confirms, mitigation path: 1) rollback kernel for affected pools, 2) patch allocator alignment to align allocations to 64KB boundaries to reduce cross-slab picks, 3) longer-term compaction.
Sara: for immediate tenant isolation, can we throttle tenant-42's burst to hard 5GB and enable quick-evict policy that favors its pages for reclaim? That would limit noisy neighbor effect.
Matt: good interim step. Anya, can you open a config change request to apply a per-tenant eviction override? Include synthetic test results.
Anya: will do. Also attaching a short perf flame: 
```\nFlame summary (heavy window): pagewalk_linear_scan ~ 15% CPU, kv_page_lookup ~ 43%, GC_reclaim ~ 5%, spin wait ~ 8%\n```
Li: CPU in pagewalks indicates wasting cycles instead of freeing memory. We should get that number down before it affects p99 latency.
Kevin: longterm, add a resident-interval metric per-tenant and a runaway detector: if residency grows while reuse_rate drops for more than N minutes, auto throttle or nudge compaction.
Sara: I'll start the shaded compaction experiment and prototype the prefetch_hint.
Anya: opening thread with links to logs and perf job: https://internal.redwood/perf/2167890250. I'll also draft the RFC for per-tenant eviction overrides.
Matt: thanks everyone. Let’s aim for a small mitigation (burst cap + coalesced frees) this week and the A/B kernel test results in 24h.
InfraBot: note: incident-alert suppressed for this thread.
Kevin: one more note — check the batcher heuristics: if the batcher delays flushes to improve throughput, it can hold KV references longer and worsen this. Add batch_drain_age to the repro checklist.
Anya: added batch_drain_age=30ms to repro. Re-running now.
Sara: ping when you have new logs.
Anya: will update here.
